text:
Maya Cheng: Heads up — we're trying to wire trace-derived SLOs for API/console routes. Question: can we rely on spans from OTLP to compute p95/p99 latency SLOs, or do we need a separate metric export?
Kevin Ortiz: short answer: you can, but it's painful if you try to run computations on raw spans at query time. better to emit derived metrics at ingest.
Sarah Li: +1. OTEL collector can do metric transforms. create histograms from span.duration, label by route/model_id. then scrape those metrics for SLOs.
Maya Cheng: sketch of options: 1) full-span retention + adhoc aggregation (expensive) 2) head-based sampling + rehydrate traces for sampled errors 3) emit derived metrics on ingest (cheapest for SLOs)
Andrew Patel: also think about cardinality. we can't tag every span with full prompt hash / token_count. keep labels to route, model, region, error_code.
Kevin Ortiz: example transform config I tried yesterday: 
```
receivers:
  otlp:
processors:
  batch:
  metrics_transform:
    transforms:
      - metric_name: request_latency_ms
        from: span.duration
        type: histogram
        labels: ["http.route","model_id","region"]
exporters:
  prometheus:
```
Works pretty well for p50/p95.
Sarah Li: note: histogram buckets need planning. use log buckets 1ms..10s. also emit request_count and error_count derived metrics (counter by status).
Maya Cheng: retention question: we need p99s backfilled for long-term SLOs. proposals? full-trace retention 7d, derived metrics 90d?
Andrew Patel: +1 on that default. full traces are heavy. maybe 14d for high-tier customers. and aggressive sampling for non-error traces after 48h.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: otelcol-metrics-transform -> staging at 2025-06-18T09:30Z :rocket:
Kevin Ortiz: also watch quotas — derived metrics explode if model_id cardinality is high. consider a mapping service to canonicalize model variants before metrics.
Sarah Li: Dashboard/Console UX: we need an SLO wiring flow: pick metric (request_latency_ms p95), window (30d), target (<= 300ms), burn-rate alerts, and canary compare baseline. should be first-class in console.
Maya Cheng: for rollouts, canary should compare SLOs + error budget burn between baseline and new model using the same metric. small UI ask: show breakdown by stage (proxy / runtime / kernel) so engineers can triage latency.
Andrew Patel: telemetry export idea: send span stages as attributes: stage=proxy|runtime|kernel and span.duration per stage. that makes stacked bars in dashboard trivial.
Kevin Ortiz: operational note: edge-case p99 needs tail-sampling. implement tail-sampling processor to keep traces with latency > threshold even if sampled out earlier.
Sarah Li: Alerts: fire when burn rate > 4 for 1h OR projected budget exhaustion within 24h. keep both absolute and relative triggers.
Maya Cheng: ok action items: 1) Kevin -> prototype metrics_transform config and hist buckets (by EOD) 2) Andrew -> propose retention tiers & sampling policy doc 3) Sarah -> mockup SLO-wiring console UX (low-fidelity)
Kevin Ortiz: will do.
Sarah Li: will do mockups tomorrow.
Andrew Patel: I'll draft retention + quota numbers and bring to infra sync.
Maya Cheng: sweet. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
